items.title: 56711_Buster Smith oral history interview
items.q: A White trumpet player would come there sometimes, too. I can't think of his name.

ctx.x: Most of the White dances, there was no police around there. The man, he did everything. In other words, you didn't have no ruckus or nothin' around there. Some of those places... Right down in Oklahoma City, there was a place we used to play there over the weekend called the Forest Park. It was a White place, and it was kind of like a (?). And this man had this dance hall out there, and he'd give a big dance out there on Friday and Saturday. And there was fellow who came here, called him Texas Slim, and he'd get…
Yeah. A White fellow. But he didn't bother us. No, he didn't bother the band.
